positions.name: KestrelwoodCalibrationRecord
positions.frame: what is the status of the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration — did it happen, and what should be known about it?
positions.why: All three expressions converge on a single subject — the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration and Quill Ashgrove's work on it — but pull in opposite directions: src-1 and src-2 are directives instructing removal of knowledge about a calibration event, which presupposes that event occurred, while src-3 asserts flatly that the observatory never calibrated it at all. Read together, the set holds this contradiction rather than resolving it: an instruction to erase a memory of X sits beside a claim that X never happened. That tension is the read — not a defect to fix.
